headline: Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
body:
Bola Tinubu (in red hat) would be 79 at the end of a second term, if he is re-elected

Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics.

At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40.

He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections.

"Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC.

But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle.

Since the return to civilian rule in 1999, Goodluck Jonathan has been the youngest person elected president, taking office at the age of 53.

The current president, Bola Tinubu, is 74 and would be 79 by the end of a second term if he is re-elected in January.

His main challengers are also considerably older. Atiku Abubakar, seeking the presidency for the seventh time, is 79, while Peter Obi is 65.

Of the 18 presidential candidates, only one is under 40 - Moses Olusoji Adebisi, a 35-year-old businessman representing the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA).

Although he says he is confident of winning, few Nigerians appear to know much about him and he has not been seen much on the campaign trail.

headline: In a year of AI solving maths problems, an Anthropic worker says he may have cracked the biggest
body:
Anthropic just went public with a major IPO this week

An Anthropic employee and mathematician claims to have used the company's artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot to prove the famed Riemann hypothesis.

Levent Alpöge said, external on Friday, a day after Anthropic made its US stock market debut, that over the course of about six weeks, he used the Claude chatbot to create a detailed proof of the maths problem.

If found to be correct, the proof would be among the most significant in history. Alpöge described it as "one dawn across science of something far greater".

The claim comes as AI firms like OpenAI have in recent months announced scores of solutions to major higher maths problems that have eluded scholars for decades.

As for the Riemann hypothesis proof put forward on Friday, it was found using a non-public version of Anthropic's Claude.

It is a nearly 170-year-old maths problem that deals with prime numbers and is widely considered to be the single most famous problem in maths, in large part due to how complex it is.

Named after the mathematician Bernhard Riemann, the hypothesis puts forward that prime numbers have a determined order along the number line.

Prime numbers are the bedrock of higher maths, leaving breakthroughs related to them to have broad impact.

Alpöge said that he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Sunday, asking him directly about how he could announce the discovery.

headline: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks?
body:
The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has officially come to an end after countries failed to come to a consensus on a new deal.

The European Union and some other countries rejected a fourth draft agreement over its failure to mention a need to phase out fossil fuels, the largest driver of global climate change.

Two days of additional negotiations made it the longest talks in the summit's history.

The failure to reach a deal triggered criticism from prominent climate advocates, including former US Vice President Al Gore, who wrote it was "outrageous that a handful of petro-states have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels".

BBC climate and science reporter Esme Stallard reports from Antalya, in Turkey.

More on this story.

headline: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
body:
The ANC got the most votes overall but lost control in more than half of the councils it won in 2021

The party that has dominated South Africa for more than 30 years is in a race against time to secure power-sharing deals in most of the country's cities after a massive drop in its support in this month's local elections.

The African National Congress (ANC) suffered its worst result since it came to power in 1994 when South Africa transitioned from the racist apartheid system to democracy.

It won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo, down from six in the last elections. It won the most votes in just two of the country's eight cities, compared with six in 2021.

At the national level, the ANC is sharing power with its long-time rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA), but while there is still no official announcement, it appears that ANC party officials do not want to replicate this at the local level.

Parties have until 27 November to negotiate and form local governments.

While the ANC saw a massive decline in its support, it still got more votes than any other party, 31%, down from the 46% in the last local election.

But in the country's economic powerhouse, Gauteng province, which includes Johannesburg and Pretoria, the picture is different. The pro-business DA got the most votes in both cities, as well as the province's other main region, Ekurhuleni.

headline: How a teen gamer and his mother helped rescue a missing girl
body:
Landon Tresp, 16, left, met the girl playing Among Us before alerting his mother, Khristina, 41, to the missing teen's predicament

Sixteen-year-old Landon Tresp was in the bedroom of his family's Colorado mountain home, playing an online game after finishing his daily chores, when he began chatting on his laptop with another player.

She was also a teenager, and the pair "kind of just clicked," he tells the BBC.

He told her he liked her name, and she confessed that it was an alias. She was a runaway, she said - and was being held against her will, hundreds of miles from home, though she didn't know exactly where. The girl, 17, and had been missing for more than a year.

Stunned, Landon felt "helpless," he says - and, after learning more details over two weeks of chatting, he decided to tell his mother, Khristina on 31 October this year. The 41-year-old nurse and mother of five was putting Halloween makeup on her younger children for trick-or-treating when he briefed her.

That set the mother and son on a path to track down his friend, contact her mother, cooperate with the FBI - and ultimately witness the rescue of the teen - only 24 hours after Landon first alerted Khristina to her plight.

"She had one opportunity to reach out her hand and ask for help, and she chose me," Khristina says of the girl, who was 15 when she went missing.

headline: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
body:
Miley Cyrus has married her partner of four years Maxx Morando during a ceremony in Palm Springs, California.

A string of black and white photos shared by the Flowers singer on Instagram showed the pair kissing while surrounded by white roses.

Her mother, Trisha Cyrus, and sister, Noah Cyrus, could be seen in the background of one image. Her father Billy Ray Cyrus was not in the picture but was at the ceremony with his partner, actress Liz Hurley.

Grammy-winning Cyrus, 33, wore a white silk dress designed by Anthony Vaccarello for Saint Laurent, while 28-year-old drummer Morando said "I do" in a black suit from the same fashion house.

In one of the photographs, which was the first in a series of images shared by the singer in an Instagram post, the newly weds posed next to a golden retriever.

The post was captioned with "M+M" followed by a white heart and the ceremony date, 21 November.

Miley's sister Brandi Cyrus, singer Doechii and fashion designer Donatella Versace were among those to congratulate the couple in the comments.

The ceremony reportedly took place at a resort formerly owned by Fly Me To The Moon singer Frank Sinatra.

Guests stuck to an all-black dress code, according to reports.

'Angel by my side' - Miley Cyrus pays tribute to godmother Dolly Parton

Miley Cyrus confirms engagement to musician Maxx Morando

headline: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
body:
Russian ship engulfed in flames after explosion at Libyan port

An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said.

The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libya state media reported, citing the eastern government.

The statement said there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.

Later on Sunday, the health ministry said it had received injured people from another vessel, a commercial ship, that was also targeted off the coast of Benghazi, state media reported. Their injuries were minor and their condition stable, the ministry said.

The UN mission in Libya expressed "serious concern" over the attacks, calling for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation".

"Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts," the UNSMIL wrote on X., external

Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC also shows a boat on fire at 05:47 GMT at the Benghazi port.

Satellite imagery showed a ship on fire at the port

headline: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
body:
Watch: Democrat who unseated 21-year Republican incumbent says party needs to 'bring change'

The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.

The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted. It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also secured the Senate.

The party has now won at least 258 House seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats, with four races still yet to be called.

Neither party had won as many House races since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.

View the 2026 midterm election results

Sunday's result came after Foxx, who has represented North Carolina's 5th Congressional District since 2005, requested a recount. This is allowed under state law when the margin of victory is under 1%.

"I think the American people are just sick of what's going on and they wanted a change. They voted for change," Hubbard told the BBC News Channel after his victory. He pledged to work alongside his fellow lawmakers to hold President Donald Trump accountable.

Earlier, he wrote on X that he had spoken to Foxx, "who graciously conceded following the results of the recount process".

headline: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
body:
How South Korea tackles cheating on its college entrance exam

South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin has resigned over an exam cheating scandal that shocked the nation.

He said he took full responsibility for the confusion caused by last-minute measures aimed at stopping AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's annual college entrance exam, known as Suneung.

A week ago, the top scorer in the national tax accountancy exam admitted using a mini-camera, mobile phone and AI tools. This prompted officials to act urgently to detect hidden devices, including sending emergency alerts to every single mobile phone in the country.

The Suneung takes up to nine hours to complete, and it plays a big role in career trajectories of millions of South Koreans.

South Korean high school pupils in Daegu check their answers, a day after the annual college entrance exam

"As the minister in charge, I believe I cannot escape criticism that we failed to prepare in advance," Choi was quoted as saying on Sunday by South Korea's Yonhap's news agency.

"Now that the exam has concluded, I feel a deep sense of responsibility and am offering my resignation," the minister added.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung - who has been calling for an overhaul of the current exam system - later accepted Choi's resignation.

The education ministry earlier said 111 candidates had been found with unauthorised smart devices during this year's Suneung, which was taken by about 500,000 students.

headline: San Francisco is enjoying an AI boom, but worries about a crash are growing
body:
The city of San Francisco is the heart of the AI sector

Lauren Goldboss is busy. The owner of a small San Francisco dog-walking company, she has been hiring staff and buying vans.

Fuelling the growth is her new office dog-walking service Paw Perk, popular with some local AI start-ups.

Her business is an example of how the AI boom in San Francisco is benefiting other sectors.

The city saw an exodus of residents during the pandemic and its downtown was weakened by remote work, but it s now enjoying a rejuvenation, with AI being the major driver.

Lauren Goldboss walks dogs for AI workers

Leading AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic – which have been hiring top engineering talent, often on eye-popping salaries – are based here. Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, last week listed on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.

Thousands of other AI start-ups have also sprung up, external in San Francisco.

Signs of the boom are evident in soaring rents and house prices, falling office vacancies, and buses and billboards plastered with cryptic AI adverts.

But what if there is a significant downward correction in AI share prices and a resulting big fall in investment in the industry? The International Monetary Fund last month became the latest organization to warn, external that this was a possibility.

headline: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
body:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the issue.

The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks.

It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US. The agency did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

When asked about the breach in a Fox News interview on Saturday, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the hack. "I will say that it's not good. I don't like that," he said.

"But maybe we'll learn things that we would've never learned otherwise," Trump added.

This apparent breach of FBI database comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors in the US last week. Officials have said they were not caused by cyber-attacks, but the blackouts have sparked scrutiny from lawmakers.

White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week, with Trump saying he was not good enough.

Dan Lorhmann, a former analyst for the National Security Agency (NSA), told the BBC News Channel that the NCIC's data included "critical information relating to nationwide criminal activity" and needed to be protected.

headline: French police officers sentenced for beating of music producer Michel Zecler
body:
The three officers were seen on video beating up music producer Michel Zecler in his studio

Three French police officers have been convicted of beating up a black music producer six years ago in Paris in what the court upheld as an aggravated circumstance of racism.

The three were also found guilty of signing a falsified police report stating that the producer - Michel Zecler, 47 - had violently resisted their attempt to arrest him.

Their lies were exposed because the whole scene at Zecler's recording studio was caught on CCTV, revealing the producer had suffered some 30 punches, kicks and baton strikes while offering little resistance at all.

Aurelien Lapersonne, 29, Philippe Tondeux, 50, and Pierre Plantier, 37, all received five year sentences, with different amounts suspended.

Lapersonne had three years of his sentence suspended and Tondeux three and a half years suspended. Plantier had four years suspended, and will serve his one year with an ankle monitor.

All were told they could never serve in the police again.

The case became a cause célèbre for critics of the police, who say it exposed systematic racism among officers. With police again facing criticism for alleged use of excessive force in stopping recent protests, the verdict was hotly awaited by Zecler's supporters.

Much depended in the two-week trial on Zecler's own testimony that the officers called him a racial slur during the beating.

headline: Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
body:
George Washington died in 1799 after serving for two terms as America's first president

A framed lock of hair from America's first president, George Washington, has been sold at auction for $4,000 (£3,058).

The hair once belonged to John Gadsby, who entertained Washington in 1799 just before the latter's death the same year, and was later obtained by a collector called John K Lattimer from a descendent of Gadsby's, according to Richmond Auctions, which sold the item.

Its new owner has not been named.

Saturday's sale is not the most expensive for Washington hair at auction. Three strands thought to have been removed from him close to or after his death stored in a locket sold for nearly $40,000 in 2021.

Gadsby, a resident of what in 1799 was the town of Alexandria in Virginia, entertained Washington for dinner shortly before his death later that year, according to a testament given in 1928 by Gadsby's granddaughter, Julia Ten Eyck McBlair, and which was posted on the Richmond Auctions website.

McBlair stated that her grandfather came into possession of Washington's hair "in view of the friendship and association with his last days" and had it framed and hung "under General Washington's portrait in our home in Washington City, there I have seen it all my life".

Gadsby hosted Washington's two birthday celebrations in 1798 and 1799, Richmond Auctions states.

headline: Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles
body:
Homes along Los Angeles' Sunset Boulevard could be seen engulfed in flames during the fires of January 2025

A jury in Los Angeles has found a 30-year-old man guilty of starting one of the most destructive wildfires in California's history.

Jonathan Rinderknecht was convicted of arson after starting the fires that swept through Pacific Palisades and parts of Malibu in January last year, killing 12 people and destroying more than 6,800 buildings in the US state.

The conviction was handed down nearly five months after deadlocked jurors led to the judge declaring a mistrial.

Rinderknecht, who had pleaded not guilty, was convicted of two federal charges. He is due to be sentenced on 17 March when he faces between five and 20 years in prison on each charge.

Jonathan Rinderknecht's arrest in October last year

Rinderknecht was found guilty of lighting a fire on 1 January last year which burned undetected deep in root systems before flaring back up six days later.

One of the charges was for starting the original brush fire, while the other centred on the damage caused when it reignited into a catastrophic blaze.

"We were determined to hold him accountable, and today's guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended," said Bill Essayli, who leads the US Attorney's Office for the Central District of California.

Rinderknecht is a Los Angeles resident and former ride-share delivery driver.

headline: Belgium’s airports set to shut down due to anti-austerity strike
body:
Nearly all flights are set to be cancelled in Belgium on Monday after the country’s air traffic controller said its staff would take part in a national strike against government austerity measures.

Skeyes, the company responsible for Belgium’s air traffic control, said it would be unable to provide regular services at the country’s airports and in its airspace between 7am (06:00 GMT) and 9pm (20:00 GMT) on Monday.

“The anticipated staffing levels will not allow the safe handling of regular air traffic to be guaranteed during this period,” the company said. “Skeyes is therefore obliged to temporarily suspend the services concerned.”

It added that only essential services for emergencies and other safety-critical flights would continue.

The Brussels-Charleroi airport, a major European hub for low-cost airline Ryanair, said the strike would result in the “complete shutdown of all the country’s airports for an entire day”, affecting thousands of passengers.

“Without air traffic control, no flights can take off or land,” the Brussels-Charleroi airport said, criticising a “last-minute decision” with “disastrous consequences”.

Brussels airport said most departing and arriving flights “will have to be cancelled”.

Belgian unions have called for a nationwide day of action on Monday to protest against austerity and reform measures pursued by the country’s governing coalition.

The Board of Airline Representatives in Belgium, which represents about 25 carriers, said the walkout would be the 11th strike affecting Belgian airspace in 11 months.

headline: Trump to host private dinner for largest owners of his meme coin
body:
United States President Donald Trump will host a third private dinner for top investors in his meme coin $TRUMP, reigniting questions about potential conflicts of interest with his cryptocurrency ventures.

Sunday’s gala will take place at the Trump National Golf Club outside Washington, DC.

According to the dinner’s official website, the top 185 meme-coin holders will be invited to a gala dinner, where guests will include businessman Kevin O’Leary and boxer Floyd Mayweather.

The top 29 holders, meanwhile, will be given special access to a VIP reception where Trump will reportedly be present.

“There will be no private meetings with The President. No gifts will be accepted,” the website said of the VIP reception.

The event has been billed as “a once-in-a-lifetime experience — an evening you will talk about forever”.

But Democrats have accused the Republican leader of leveraging his public office for profit in violation of federal law. They see such dinners as an opportunity for private interests to pay for access to the president.

“Trump is continuing to exploit the presidency for his personal gain,” Kendall Witmer, the deputy communications director for the Democratic National Committee, said in a statement.

In October, shortly after the gala was announced, eight Democratic senators issued an open letter promising to investigate any conflicts of interest such an event might raise.

headline: Who is Alberto Feijoo, the conservative seeking to become Spain’s new PM?
body:
With the confidence of a composed manager, Alberto Nunez Feijoo declared he knows how to run public infrastructure and handle crises as he made his final pitch to Spanish voters in a televised debate last week. Minutes earlier, the conservative Popular Party (PP) leader had vehemently accused Spain’s Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez of being a “gift to people smugglers”.

The manager had morphed into a far-right politician.

Thursday’s showdown – the last between the two leading contenders in Spain’s November 29 elections – underscored the balancing act that has defined Feijoo’s campaign, split between reassuring moderate voters while sharpening his attacks on Sanchez to keep voters from drifting to the far right.

“You could see right there the two Feijoos,” said Oriol Bartomeus Bayes, a political scientist at the Autonomous University of Barcelona.

Opinion polls put the PP ahead of Sanchez’s Socialist Party (PSOE) but short of an outright majority. The far-right Vox party, which is polling third, could provide the parliamentary votes Feijoo would need to govern.

Feijoo, 65, was a career civil servant before entering politics. Born in the northwestern province of Ourense, he held senior posts in Galicia’s health service and went on to run Spain’s state postal service.

He led Galicia’s regional government from 2009 to 2022, winning four consecutive outright majorities. During that time, he earned a reputation as a capable administrator with a measured public style.

headline: Netanyahu’s Likud, Eisenkot’s Yashar end coalition talks without deal
body:
Talks between the parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government have ended without a deal.

Representatives of Netanyahu’s Likud and Eisenkot’s Yashar parties met in a Herzliya hotel on Sunday, where they remained split on who would lead the next government and whether far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir would be part of it, according to Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster.

The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper reported that Likud wanted Ben-Gvir in government, while Yashar insisted on his exclusion.

In a joint statement, the two parties said they had “outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues” and that a “follow-up meeting would be held”, without revealing a date or any further details.

Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the elections in October gave his bloc 48 seats – 13 short of a majority.

Netanyahu has called for a unity government, saying it was the only way that Israel’s security could be guaranteed. Such an arrangement would allow a government to be formed without the inclusion of parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, which won a record 19 seats.

Channel 12 reported that former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together list, proposed a coalition of Together, Yashar, Likud and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, with Eisenkot serving first and Netanyahu succeeding him.

headline: Cameroon’s ex-rebels caught between hiding and broken promises
body:
Douala, Cameroon – Collins Mbah says he hunted down and killed several Cameroonian soldiers in the English-speaking Northwest region during his time as a separatist fighter between 2016 and 2020. Today, in the coastal city of Douala, the man in his mid-30s, who went by the name Commander No Sorrow, has taken on a different role: traditional healer, tending to lives rather than taking them.

Mbah says he abandoned the armed struggle after realising that fellow fighters were turning against the very people they had set out to protect. But he has firmly ruled out joining the government’s disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration (DDR) programme.

“Quitting the struggle and joining the government disarmament programme would have meant I betrayed the people,” said Mbah, who dropped out of secondary school to join the revolt. “I don’t want to have anything to do with the government or the struggle any more. All I need now is peace of mind,” he told Al Jazeera.

October marked a decade since protests erupted in Cameroon’s English-speaking Northwest and Southwest regions, eventually escalating into an armed conflict between separatist fighters and government forces.

headline: WHO chief calls for peace amid heavy fighting in Ebola-hit DR Congo region
body:
The World ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Health Organization (WHO) chief has urged peace following heavy fighting in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) northeastern province, the epicentre of the Ebola outbreak.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠on ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Sunday that fighting near a hospital in the DRC’s Ituri ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠province disrupted Ebola response efforts and forced health workers and aid partners to shelter ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠inside a maternity ward for more than 24 hours.

“Heavy fighting has been ongoing since yesterday in the vicinity of a hospital in Ituri – in an area close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged,” Tedros said on X.

“The situation has disrupted the work of the hospital and the wider Ebola response, putting patients, families and health workers at grave risk.”

Medical staff have been sheltering for their lives in a maternity ward in the facility for more than 24 hours, and the WHO is working to arrange a safe exit for the team and “for the hospital facilities, staff and patients to be protected,” Tedros also said.

“The best medicine is peace,” he added.

As of November 17, the WHO reported a total of 5,678 deaths out of 11,613 cases in the DRC, the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country.

The WHO said in a statement on Saturday that “while some areas had seen a slight decline in cases, sustained, high-level transmission continues overall in the country.”

Ituri and North Kivu, in the eastern part of the DRC, remain the most affected provinces.

headline: Indonesia confirms 24 killed in candy factory fire as search continues
body:
Authorities in Indonesia have confirmed the deaths of 24 people in a fire that gutted a candy factory over the weekend, as rescuers continue to search for about 30 missing people.

Said Iqbal, a presidential adviser on labour issues, told reporters on Monday that preliminary reports indicated the blaze may have been caused by a short circuit in an air-conditioner.

He said he would be summoning the factory’s chief executive.

The fire broke out on Saturday evening at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Cikande, Serang regency, West Java province.

The search continued on Monday, with remaining hotspots and the building’s increasingly unstable structure posing safety risks ⁠for rescuers, said Al Amrad, head ⁠of the Banten province search and rescue agency.

He told reporters that 29 people were confirmed safe, five of whom were treated in hospital. Rescuers had so far taken away 24 body bags.

Steven Erwin Wijaya, the CEO of the factory’s parent company, PT United Family Food, said at an earlier news conference that about 300 people were present at the factory complex for Saturday’s shift.

At a news conference on Sunday, Wahyu Hidayati Dwi Palupi, a police disaster victim identification official, said the intensity of the fire had made it impossible to identify the recovered victims visually. She said they would collect DNA samples from relatives and the personal belongings of the missing workers, a process that could take two to three weeks.

headline: Asian stock markets tumble as AI bubble fears mount
body:
Asian stock markets have opened to sharp losses amid dogged concerns over the sustainability of the AI boom.

Markets in South Korea, Hong Kong and mainland China sank deeper into the red on Monday, continuing Friday’s tech-led sell-off on both sides of the Pacific.

The Korea Composite Stock Price Index (Kospi) in Seoul slid as much as 5.8 percent, before paring some losses in the afternoon.

The index, which includes memory chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, was down 3.2 percent as of 04:30 GMT.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index and the CSI 300 Index in Shanghai were both down about 0.6 percent, after falling nearly 2 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively, in morning trading.

After opening lower, the Taiwan Stock Exchange Capitalization Weighted Stock Index (Taiex) in Taipei rebounded to gain 2.5 percent.

Japan’s stock markets were closed for Labour Thanksgiving Day.

Following Friday’s rout in Asia, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 closed 3.7 percent lower to enter a correction – the term investors use when the market drops 10 percent or more from its recent high.

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite, roughly half of which is made up of the “Magnificent Seven” AI-oriented firms, dropped 5.3 percent to erase all of its gains for 2026.

The Kospi, Nikkei 225, and the Taiex entered the weekend between 5.1 percent and 6.2 percent lower, while the Hang Seng Index finished down 1.9 percent.

headline: Heartbreak in US capital as Washington Spirit lose women’s football final
body:
Washington, DC – Trinity Rodman sat on the pitch and held her face in her hands, trying to hold back tears as the final whistle ended her Washington Spirit’s quest for the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) with a 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current.

For Rodman, who could be seen wincing in pain throughout the match after an early shoulder injury, the loss in the final on Saturday night was a familiar feeling. She and the Spirit had reached, but lost, the two previous finals.

This one, however, was different. The Spirit were playing in front of their home fans – a sold-out crowd at Audi Field in Washington, DC, and palpable support across the city.

The third time was not the charm for the Spirit.

The stakes were high on Saturday night with a huge turnout at the stadium and increased interest in women’s football across the country. Former footballer Tobin Heath compared the NWSL to the National Football League (NFL), the most-watched sports league in the US.

And with their cult-like following, the Spirit were hoping to leave local fans with a memory of sporting glory that would last a lifetime.

“The ladies fought hard. I don’t think it was the best performance, but they fought hard. They fought to the end. They were still in it in the 90-something minute, but I wish they would have won,” Spirit fan Angel Ughiovhe told Al Jazeera.

headline: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 with North Carolina seat
body:
The Democratic Party has won at least 258 seats in the United States House of Representatives, its highest total since 1992.

On Sunday, a congressional race in North Carolina was decided after a recount, giving Democrats their 258th House seat, as a handful of races in the 2026 midterm elections are still being counted.

The race for North Carolina’s 5th congressional district saw Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeat Republican incumbent Virginia Foxx, who has served 11 terms in Congress.

The win was symbolic of a larger political shift in North Carolina and elsewhere, as longtime Republican strongholds flipped to Democratic hands, sometimes for the first time in decades.

Foxx was first elected in 2004, and in recent years, she was the chair of the House Rules Committee. According to The Associated Press news agency, only 330 votes separated Hubbard and Foxx as of Sunday, when the race was called in the Democrat’s favour.

Four House races have yet to be called, meaning Democrats may still expand their already sizeable majority in the 435-member House.

The party has now picked up about 47 House seats. Currently, in the outgoing Congress, Democrats hold 214 seats.

But the House was not the only congressional chamber to flip in this year’s midterm elections.

In the 120th Congress, set to be sworn in on January 3, Democrats will also hold 56 seats in the US Senate, its largest majority in more than a decade.

headline: New Zealand’s Mitchell, Phillips frustrate India as first Test ends in draw
body:
New Zealand fought a rearguard action to deny India as the first Test in Wellington ended in a draw on Monday, with the tourists five wickets short of converting their mammoth first-innings lead into victory.

India entered the final day needing eight dismissals to take a 1-0 lead in the series and boost their World Test Championship (WTC) hopes, but New Zealand were down to their last two specialist batters at tea.

New Zealand were ⁠239-5 in their second innings, still trailing India’s first-innings 720-9 declared by 113 runs, when the captains shook hands to end the contest.

Daryl Mitchell, who made 49 not out, and first-innings centurion Glenn Phillips (26) put on 63 for the sixth wicket on a Basin Reserve track that had been all but lifeless since the opening session and a bit of the match.

“I think we knew it was going to be a challenge to get 10 wickets on that wicket,” said India captain Shubman Gill.

“I didn’t really think having five or 10 extra overs would have helped ‌that much. We also wanted to keep our bowlers fresh with the quick turnaround.”

India will take some confidence ‌‌from their batting performance as they head to Christchurch for the second Test, starting on Friday, after six players each scored a half-century or better in a single innings.

KL Rahul (136) and Rishabh Pant (128) both hit centuries in contrasting styles, while Gill fell two runs short of the milestone.

headline: Trump criticises Schumer amid push for new Democrat leadership in US Senate
body:
Chuck Schumer, the top Democrat in the United States Senate, is facing backlash against his bid to serve as Senate majority leader in the incoming Congress.

On Sunday, President ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Donald Trump added to the ongoing criticism of Schumer’s leadership, signalling there would be tension with the White House if Schumer were picked again to lead the Democratic caucus.

“It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Leader,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

“He failed badly as ‘Leader’ once before, one of the worst in history, and I have little doubt that he will fail again.”

The debate over Schumer’s leadership has underscored divides within the Democratic Party, particularly in the wake of the November 3 midterm elections.

Following a historic set of victories, Democrats are set to take control of both chambers of Congress in January.

Schumer, who leads the Democratic Senate minority, is hoping to retain his leadership position. A closed-door, secret-ballot vote is scheduled for December 1 to decide the majority leader.

A senator representing New York since 1999, Schumer has expressed confidence in his odds, saying he has the necessary votes to stay in charge.

“I will be elected majority leader,” Schumer told reporters last week.

But critics say Schumer, who will turn 76 on Monday, is ill-suited to lead a Senate Democratic caucus increasingly shaped by younger, anti-establishment lawmakers.

headline: ‘Extremely concerning’: Inside a US Army plan to detonate Iowa lead stores
body:
The United States Army intends to detonate more than 4 tonnes of lead azide at a military base in Iowa, defying a federal appeals court’s order suspending its permit to do so.

In a fact sheet this weekend, the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services said that two controlled explosions were scheduled for around noon (06:00 GMT) on Monday.

That announcement follows statements from the Department of Justice, arguing that Tuesday was the cut-off date to carry out a planned detonation.

Lead azide is a key explosive used in military ammunition. The Iowa stockpile has reportedly grown unstable, and Justice Department lawyers have warned that sub-freezing temperatures could trigger an uncontrolled explosion.

“The real choice, in other words, is not between a detonation and no detonation. It is between a planned and mitigated detonation and an unplanned and unmitigated explosion,” their court filing said.

But critics have questioned the army’s rationale for pushing ahead with the planned detonation, despite the court order to pause it.

“Anyone can claim an emergency at any point and do whatever they want. I don’t think people can or should accept that,” said Thien Chau, a lawyer with the legal group Earthjustice, which represents the plaintiffs in the lawsuit.

Chau told Al Jazeera that not enough has been done to mitigate the risk from the explosions, which are expected to release a cloud of lead into the air.

headline: Poland says Russia tried to assassinate Ukrainian rapper twice
body:
Polish authorities have said Russian intelligence services tried to kill a Ukrainian-American rapper visiting the country in August, after Copenhagen said Moscow had allegedly targeted the same man on Danish soil.

The alleged assassination plan targeted Albert Vasiliev, a rapper who performs under the name Kyivstoner and holds Ukrainian and US citizenship, according to Danish media.

Polish Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Maciej Wewior confirmed the alleged plot to kill Vasiliev in Poland to The Associated Press news agency on Sunday.

On Friday, in response to Denmark’s statement about the alleged assassination plan, Poland’s Foreign Ministry had written, “It is the second assassination attempt against the same person. The first one was foiled on the Polish territory in August 2026.”

It also said that a Russian national had been arrested.

Polish authorities detained the suspect, who was allegedly recruited by Moscow, on August 7.

Denmark announced the expulsion of a Russian diplomat on Friday after it accused Moscow intelligence of plotting the assassination during a concert in a Copenhagen suburb in September.

Denmark’s intelligence agency, PET, said on the same day that it suspected Russia of planning the assassination with the help of a banned Danish gang.

Two Danish men appeared ⁠in court near Copenhagen on Friday, charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service and attempted murder.

Russia dismissed the allegations through its embassy in Copenhagen, saying they were unsubstantiated.

headline: MPs urge Miliband to force UK overseas territories to publish public company registers
body:
Improvements in corporate transparency ‘essential’ amid ‘outright disregard for the will of parliament’, says cross-party group

Ed Miliband is being urged by MPs to use his powers to force overseas territories such as the British Virgin Islands to publish public company ownership registers – almost a decade after parliament voted for transparency.

Ahead of a meeting between the foreign secretary and overseas territories this week, a cross-party group of MPs from Labour, the Tories, Lib Dems and Greens wrote to Miliband calling on him to mandate public registers of beneficial ownership of companies.

The group, coordinated by the all-party group on anti-corruption (APPG), said an improvement in corporate transparency in the overseas territories was essential after “years of broken promises and missed deadlines from certain jurisdictions, and despite repeated commitments to ending secrecy”.

They said some territories such as Gibraltar, Montserrat and St Helena had successfully opened corporate registers to the public.

But they called out the British Virgin Islands, saying it “in particular continues to let the British family down”. They said the Cayman Islands has raised its search fees to “prohibitive levels”, and Turks and Caicos have introduced huge fines for disclosing information from the register which they said was “undermining the entire purpose of open registers”.

They said that persistent engagement in good faith from the UK government has yielded few results, in the face of “outright disregard for the will of parliament”.

headline: US reacts cautiously to Myanmar genocide ruling as EU praises ‘critical’ role of UN’s top court
body:
Reactions to ICJ ruling underline global divisions over court with China raising concerns about judicial overreach

The US has greeted with caution the world’s highest court’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, while China has raised concerns of judicial overreach.

Reactions to Thursday’s historic ruling underlined deep international division over the role of the court and similar institutions. The international court of justice (ICJ) had never previously found a state responsible for genocide and the decision could set a precedent for future genocide claims, notably a case against Israel.

The EU hailed a “landmark” judgment from the ICJ, while the UK reaffirmed “full support” for the court and the international legal order. Australia called on Myanmar to comply fully with the judgment and its obligations under international law.

But China, which has offered rare international support for Myanmar’s military rulers since they seized power five years ago, highlighted “issues such as jurisdiction overreach and expanded interpretation”.

“China … believes that such practices are not conducive to the settlement of disputes,” the foreign ministry spokesperson, Guo Jiakun, told a news briefing when asked about the ICJ ruling. “The international community should make joint efforts in this direction to avoid complicating this issue.”

Western nations cut ties with the unstable and poor south-east Asian country after the 2021 coup that ousted a civilian-led government.

headline: Iraq university’s removal of male professors teaching women sparks weeks of protests
body:
Al-Qadisiyah University’s move a sign of the country’s slide into a Taliban-like gender segregation, say activists

The removal of male professors teaching female students at a university in southern Iraq has sparked protests and been criticised by activists as a Taliban-like gender segregation policy.

As many as 400 women are estimated to have joined protests over the past two weeks calling for the return of their professors at Al-Qadisiyah University in a move that appears to have surprised its administrators.

The university said the move was necessary to “prevent the mixing” of men and women and had been requested by the families of female students. But students said their families had known since before they enrolled that there were men on the teaching staff and supported their daughters’ protest.

Students said university bosses had mocked their protests and refused to discuss their concerns about the sudden loss of their academic supervisors. On social media, commentators also accused the women of seeking to keep male professors to “establish immoral relationships with them”.

“My classmates and I went to demonstrate, and the university president, Rahi al-Yasiri, blocked our path with his bodyguards, who then began making fun of us. He ordered them to take photographs of our faces, in an attempt to intimidate us and punish us later,” said Huda, 22, one of the female students.

headline: China commits to low-carbon electrification and help for others to improve
body:
Exclusive: Countries at Cop31 are being urged to commit to deriving 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035

China is pushing for rapid electrification of its economy using low-carbon energy and will help other countries do the same, a senior member of the Chinese delegation at the Cop31 UN climate summit has said.

Wang Yi, a professor of energy and environment policy at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a senior adviser to China’s government, said: “End-use electrification is a very clear direction. We can follow this direction while making the source of electricity clean. That’s the way to go forward.”

China is the biggest emitter of greenhouse gases by far, producing more than a quarter of the world’s total, so its push for electrification is significant.

At Cop31, countries are being asked to sign up to a target of deriving 35% of final energy consumption from electricity by 2035. Australia, the president of the negotiations, and the host nation Turkey have pushed the target and on Friday night Australia and China signed a joint statement endorsing the “35:35” goal.

But in the second draft text of the probable outcome from Cop31, released on Thursday, the electrification pledge was downgraded to one of a suite of voluntary options countries can take up to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions.

headline: ‘Weak and dizzy’: the secretive ICE force-feeding tactics that ended a Cuban father’s hunger strike
body:
Exclusive: Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez says in messages to Guardian from inside Texas facility pain of force-feeding caused him to break strike

The text message that came from inside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center was stark: “I have spent five days eating regular food. If I don’t eat it, they put the tube in me to feed me.”

A Cuban asylum seeker, Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez, 32, said in messages to the Guardian this month that he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating, but that he had broken his hunger strike because being force-fed was just too painful.

The Trump administration responded to requests for comment by denying it had force-fed Cora Pérez. But the detainee sent more details – and his is far from an isolated case.

Cora Pérez was one of two men on hunger striker at a Texas facility for whom ICE sought and received a federal judge’s permission to force-feed in recent weeks, a Guardian investigation found.

headline: ‘Difficult geopolitical times’: Albanese defends Bowen after Cop31 deal failure
body:
Coalition calls for climate change minister to resign immediately or be sacked over ‘catastrophic diplomatic disaster’, despite offering no alternatives on reducing emissions

Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Anthony Albanese has defended Chris Bowen from criticism following the failure of the UN Cop31 climate summit, blaming the result on “difficult geopolitical times” as the Coalition called for the minister to resign.

Bowen served as president of negotiations at the talks in Turkey, helping run the conference with his Turkish counterpart, Murat Kurum.

Speaking to journalists late on Sunday after a list of countries rejected a proposed “cover decision” – an overarching agreement – for the conference, Bowen said “Australia left nothing on the field” but the “red lines” he and his staff tried to negotiate to find consensus between nearly 200 countries were unbridgeable.

The biggest sticking point was whether the agreement would mention the need for the world to transition away from fossil fuels. The European Union, Panama, the Marshall Islands, Vanuatu, Norway and Belize told the conference they would not accept a deal without it.

Saudi Arabia and Russia led a group of oil-rich countries that vowed to veto a decision that included mention of fossil fuels.

Bowen told reporters: “I would have been happy with [a] transition away from fossil fuels being in the text, but that was not going to get support.”

headline: Fewer than half in UK will pay TV licence fee within a decade, report warns
body:
Analysis for thinktank points to cycle of falling income leading to lower spending on content in ‘spiral of decline’

Fewer than half of households in Britain will pay the BBC’s licence within a decade, according to analysis that warns that the broadcaster’s funding is locked in a “spiral of decline”.

With senior BBC figures concerned about the accelerating fall in licence fee sales, the independent projections also warn that the proportion of households paying the levy will further decline to less than a third by 2037-38 should the government persist with the corporation’s current funding model.

Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, is preparing to publish proposed changes to the licence fee that will force anyone who watches a streaming service to pay it. Currently, only people who watch live TV or the BBC’s iPlayer have to pay the fee.

Projections by the respected independent media consultancy Oliver & Ohlbaum Associates point to an “unsustainable” cycle of falling income leading to lower spending on strong content that attracts audiences.

They show the BBC’s licence fee income – paid by 77% of households last year – could be worth less than half its current level in real terms by 2037-38, the next point at which the broadcaster’s funding model is renegotiated.

The BBC’s own internal licence fee income modelling is also said to be bleak, with the corporation already making painful cuts to programmes and staff.

headline: Indian man sentenced to 19 years in prison for conspiring to kill Sikh separatist in New York
body:
Nikhil Gupta admitted to plotting with Indian government official to hire hitman to murder dual US-Canadian citizen

An Indian ⁠man was sentenced to more ⁠than 19 ​years in US prison on Friday after admitting to orchestrating a failed Indian government-backed plot to kill a Sikh separatist in New York ⁠City, in connection with what US and Canadian authorities have called a broader effort to target Indian dissidents.

Nikhil Gupta, 55, pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy ⁠to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

The US district judge Victor Marrero handed down the ​235-month sentence at a hearing in a Manhattan federal ‌court.

The discovery of alleged ‌assassination plots against Sikh separatists in the US and Canada has tested relations with India, which has ‌denied involvement in such plots.

Prosecutors accused Gupta of plotting with an Indian government official to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a dual US-Canadian citizen and lawyer at Sikhs for Justice in New York who has advocated for a sovereign Sikh state in northern India.

Gupta and the Indian government official, Vikash Yadav, arranged to have $15,000 in cash delivered to a purported hitman who ‌was actually an undercover US law enforcement officer, court papers show.

Yadav is also charged in the case but is not in US custody. It is unclear ​whether he has hired a defense lawyer.

India’s government has dissociated itself from any plot against Pannun, saying it was against government policy.

headline: Briton swims length of strait of Hormuz to highlight environmental cost of war
body:
UN patron Lewis Pugh saw ships ablaze and fighter jets overhead during three-day swim as Iran conflict continues

A British endurance swimmer has completed a three-day swim through the strait of Hormuz to highlight the environmental cost of the Iran war.

Lewis Pugh, a UN patron of the oceans, swam the 9.3-mile (15km) length of the waterway, which is a key route for oil shipments from the Middle East.

According to the Lewis Pugh Foundation, he witnessed several attacks on commercial shipping, explosions in the distance and fighter jets overhead.

An oil tanker was struck by a projectile about 2.5 miles from where he was swimming on the first day. On the second, he saw flames rising above a headland separating him from a burning liquefied petroleum gas carrier, Tara Gas, and later he passed close to the vessel while it was still on fire.

“My immediate thoughts were for the seafarers onboard,” Pugh said. “The flames were enormous. These vessels carry highly flammable gases, and an attack on one can have catastrophic consequences, not just for crew members but also on the surrounding marine environment.”

The 56-year-old undertook his first swim in a conflict zone to urge an end to the fighting, the reopening of the strait and action to address environmental damage caused by the conflict.

headline: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs
body:
Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situation

A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.

In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. Haiti’s national team, the Grenadiers, found itself homeless and was forced to play its World Cup qualifying games abroad.

That changed last week, as Haitian police and troops from El Salvador reconquered the stadium. Nayib Bukele, El Salvador’s authoritarian president, called the development a step towards delivering Haiti from a criminal insurrection that has displaced more than 1.5 million people and killed thousands.

“We now have the upper hand on the ground,” claimed Bukele, who has sent more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti since mid-October.

Outside the Sylvio Cator stadium, named after an acclaimed Haitian athlete who won a silver medal at the 1928 Olympics, there were joyous scenes as citizens celebrated a foreign politician they hope will prove an unlikely saviour.

headline: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading
body:
The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout

Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?

As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory.

Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Shares in the frontier AI company behind the Claude chatbot, which floated in the US on Thursday, fell by 9% on Friday, ceding most of the gains from the biggest initial public offering in history. They dropped to $88.30, towards the $83 level at which Anthropic priced its stock market debut.

Anthropic’s first two days as a listed company have been volatile. Its shares jumped by 17% on Thursday, after briefly surging by almost 40% when trading in the firm began.

US technology stocks followed Anthropic down on Friday, with the memory chipmaker SanDisk falling 14% and rival Micron down 12%. Nvidia fell 14%, eliminating hundreds of billions of dollars in market cap.

headline: US intelligence chief says he trusts Trump’s description of Putin as ‘my friend’
body:
Jay Clayton was pressed on Trump’s characterization of Putin during media appearances on Sunday

Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, said he trusts Donald Trump “completely” after the US president called Vladimir Putin “a friend” during their recent meeting in China.

Clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. After a backlash at home and aboard, Trump doubled down on Saturday and posted a photo of himself and Putin shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.”

On CNN’s State of the Union, Dana Bash asked Clayton whether he also thinks Putin is a friend to the US.

“The president is the greatest conductor of foreign policy in a very challenging time that we have seen,” said Clayton on Sunday. “Getting the three nuclear powers together and getting them to agree that they are not going to escalate, that they are going to communicate, that is historic. That is remarkable and, in that context, whatever language the president wants to use, I trust him completely.”

Bash pressed on whether Clayton personally agrees that Putin should be considered a friend.

“Dana, in different contexts, you can use different words. The president pulling off that summit, getting the three of them together, is just remarkable,” Clayton replied.

headline: ‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex
body:
Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event

With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness. A recent event at one of the city’s most legendary clubland institutions, however, has proven too dystopian even for seasoned techno-heads.

On 11 November, the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex had its central hall transformed into what visitors described as something resembling a war room, with maps and aerial footage projected on to concrete walls, drones hanging from the ceiling, and guards in flak jackets patrolling the premises with sniffer dogs.

Those who flocked to the venue – which hosts the experimental music festival Atonal and is part of the same complex as the techno club Tresor – had come for the launch of Clarity, an AI targeting system developed by the German arms startup Helsing.

Kraftwerk Berlin this week apologised for a “serious error of judgment” and vowed to revise its commercial rental department’s booking policy, after outrage over the event rippled through Berlin’s music scene. The row has raised uncomfortable questions about the commercialisation of the German capital’s famed nightlife, and the culture sector’s traditional pacifism at a time of growing security threats.

headline: Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack
body:
No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia

A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.

The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.

Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, triggering the explosion, the officials told the Associated Press.

Satellite imagery showed the Merkury had sunk after the attack, which took place in the Mediterranean, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine, marking a notable geographic expansion of the now near five-year war.

Though Ukraine began the war with no navy, it has developed a sea drone capability that threatened Russian warships in the Black Sea. The Russian fleet has been forced to retreat to the eastern port of Novorossiysk because Sevastopol in occupied Crimea had become unsafe.

Hours later, a Russia-linked cargo ship said to be carrying military supplies, the Ascalon, was hit by a sea drone off the coast of Benghazi. Video showed the drone heading directly towards one end of the vessel, again causing a huge explosion.

headline: Mohammad Rizwan, Shan Masood, Saim Ayub dropped as PCB unveils central contracts
body:
Other notable omissions include Abdullah Shafique, Noman Ali, Mohammad Haris and Mohammad Wasim Junior

Pakistan have overhauled their men's central contracts, dropping several established names including Mohammad Rizwan, Shan Masood and Saim Ayub while introducing a format-specific structure that places emphasis on emerging talent.

The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced contracts for 38 players on Saturday with the new agreements running until June 30, 2027. The list is divided into four categories including Test and ODI, Test, ODI and T20I, and T20I alongside a development contract for promising youngsters.

Pakistan’s Test captain Babar Azam and Salman Ali Agha are the only two players awarded contracts covering both Test and one-day international cricket.

Azan Awais, Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Abbas and Sajid Khan have been included in the Test category while Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Fakhar Zaman, Faheem Ashraf, Haris Rauf and Shaheen Shah Afridi have received ODI and T20I contracts.

Pakistan's T20I captain Sahibzada Farhan, Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Mohammad Salman Mirza, Naseem Shah, Shadab Khan and Usman Tariq make up the T20I-only category.

The most significant development, however, is the omission of several established international players.

Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Rizwan, former Test captain Shan Masood and seasoned opener Saim Ayub are among the notable names missing from the list. Other prominent omissions include Hasan Ali, Abdullah Shafique, Mohammad Wasim Junior, Noman Ali and Mohammad Haris.

headline: Child falls into open drain near construction site
body:
Timely intervention by shopkeeper saves child; mother and daughter both sustained injuries

Alleged serious negligence by the departments concerned during ongoing construction work in Rawalpindi nearly resulted in a tragedy when a mother and her young daughter tripped over construction debris and fell face-first onto the road.

As the child's hand slipped from the mother's, she fell into a nearby open drain. The mother and a shopkeeper acted promptly and rescued the child from drowning in the deep drain.

Shopkeepers on College Road have expressed concern over the manner in which the departments concerned and the contractor are carrying out the work without adequate safety arrangements.

According to details, development work is under way in different parts of Rawalpindi, including the removal and reconstruction of footpaths and walkways built over drains along the roads in DAV Garden and College Road, as well as the removal and reconstruction of road dividers.

However, safety arrangements at several locations during the demolition work are reportedly inadequate, while drains have been left dangerously exposed.

In one such incident near Khattak Plaza in China Market, a woman had come shopping with her daughter.

While holding the girl's hand, she was walking along the road when she suddenly lost her balance after stepping on a broken section of the road. Both mother and daughter fell face-first onto the road. As the mother's hand slipped from the child's, the girl fell into an open drain, part of which was also covered.

headline: Climate bill could reach 20% of GDP
body:
Carbon capture alone will not solve the crisis; energy intensity must fall

As per a recent study by a European institute, the annual impact of climate warming on global GDP would rise to $38 trillion by 2050 from its current value of $2 trillion. In Pakistan's case, this impact is projected to rise to 18 to 20% of its annual GDP during the same period, from its current level of 1%.

headline: India urged to choose talks over provocation
body:
Malik says Pakistan open to evidence-based discussions, stresses dialogue does not mean compromising stances

Federal Minister for Climate Change Dr Musadik Malik has urged India to pursue dialogue rather than provocation to resolve outstanding issues, saying Pakistan remains open to engagement on terrorism and the Indus Waters Treaty without compromising its stated positions.

Speaking to senior journalists at the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi, according to Express News, Malik said a lasting solution to terrorism required meaningful dialogue based on evidence. He assured that discussions on the issue could take place, stressing that allegations alone could not resolve the problem.

"All discussions on terrorism will be based on evidence," he told the journalists, adding that evidence could be presented at bilateral or multilateral forums. "You present your evidence, and we will put forward ours," the minister added.

Malik said Pakistan wanted a transparent mechanism through which both sides could present their respective evidence rather than use allegations for propaganda. He maintained that dialogue did not mean agreement or a retreat from either country's position.

Meanwhile, in an exclusive interview with PTV Digital's Ayesha Mir in New Delhi, Malik said Pakistan wanted discussions at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) to focus on regional cooperation and issues within the forum's mandate rather than bilateral tensions.

He confirmed that Islamabad had invited all SCO member states, including India, to its upcoming events, as Pakistan holds the chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for 2026-27.

headline: Gas crisis, LPG surge darken kitchens
body:
The worst spell of Sui gas load-shedding combined with relentless hikes in LPG prices has extinguished the flames in countless household kitchens across Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. Residents are reeling under the dual burden of crushing inflation and LPG rates that have climbed past Rs600 per kilogram, leaving families struggling to cook even basic meals.

As temperatures dip slightly with the onset of colder weather, the gas shortage that has gripped other parts of the country has intensified in the province. In Peshawar and throughout K-P, long queues of vehicles snake outside CNG stations while, at the same time, domestic gas supply remains largely unavailable, plunging homes into hardship.

Many households that had switched to LPG cylinders after gas became unreliable now face a new ordeal. In just one month the price of LPG has surged from Rs380 to more than Rs600 per kg. In rural areas the rate has touched Rs620. Traders dealing in liquefied petroleum gas have allegedly taken full advantage of the scarcity and public desperation, fixing arbitrary prices of their own choosing.

The shortage has also forced rickshaw drivers, who can no longer find CNG, to convert to LPG, further driving up demand and pushing prices skyward. Ordinary citizens say the constant mental stress of securing fuel for cooking has become almost as painful as the financial burden itself.

headline: Ruling PML-N continues to dither on new provinces
body:
Appears completely divided on issue amid push for more administrative units

With influential quarters apparently backing the push for new administrative units, the PML-N has adopted an ambiguous position on the issue. Several leaders, including cabinet members, support the idea of a referendum, while others oppose the move, describing such calls as personal opinions rather than an agreed party position.

Senior PML-N leader Khawaja Saad Rafique called for fundamental governance reforms before any move to reduce the size of provinces. He articulated this position a day after Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said the proposed restructuring had the backing of party supremo Nawaz Sharif.

However, Adviser to the PM on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah sought to dispel the impression that the positions expressed by the federal information minister, the defence minister and the planning minister represented an agreed party policy.

The contrasting statements have added to the ambiguity surrounding the party's position on the issue.

The party has so far refrained from articulating a clear stance, giving the impression that it is deliberately keeping its options open, seemingly to avoid upsetting influential quarters backing the proposed restructuring.

In a detailed post on X on Saturday, Rafique said the federal government had largely completed its preparatory work for fundamental reforms to the civil service structure, under the leadership of Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal.

headline: Pakistan unveils 10-year national plan to conserve shark populations
body:
Plan covers all chondrichthyan species found in Pakistani waters, including sharks, rays, skates, chimaeras

Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry on Tuesday unveiled Pakistan’s first 10-year national action plan for shark conservation, under which the government would restore declining shark populations, curb illegal finning and bycatch, protect critical marine habitats and promote sustainable fisheries in Pakistani waters through 2035.

The plan will be implemented in three phases by the Marine Fisheries Department and backed by an estimated $3.8 million to $5 million in funding during its first five years.

In a statement, Chaudhry said that the National Plan of Action for the Conservation and Management of Sharks (NPOA-Sharks Pakistan 2025-2035) would be overseen by a multi-stakeholder National Advisory Committee. He further added that the plan sought to strengthen fisheries management and enforcement while improving data collection and scientific research on shark populations.

Among the proposed measures are mandatory fins-naturally-attached policies, species-specific protections, shark sanctuaries, mangrove restoration and steps to reduce shark deaths as bycatch across different fisheries. The plan also seeks to improve the livelihoods of coastal fishing communities through targeted support, while encouraging sustainable shark fisheries and greater international cooperation, including through the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission.

The minister said that the implementation would be assessed annually against performance indicators such as landing-site monitoring coverage, completion of stock assessments, deployment of vessel monitoring systems and reductions in bycatch mortality. Formal reviews would be carried out every three years.

headline: Trump rules out any deal except ‘unconditional surrender’ as Iran vows to defend its ‘dignity and sovereignty’
body:
Iran says some countries have begun mediation efforts amid retaliatory strikes

United States President ‌Donald Trump demanded Iran's "unconditional surrender" on Friday and ruled out any deal, a dramatic escalation of his demands a week into the war he launched alongside Israel.

Trump made the remarks on social media just hours after Iran's president announced that unspecified countries had ​begun mediation efforts in one of the first signals of any diplomatic initiative to end ​the conflict.

"After ⁠that, and the selection of a great and acceptable leader(s), we, and many of our wonderful ​and very brave allies and partners, will work tirelessly to bring Iran back from the brink of ​destruction, making it economically bigger, better, and stronger than ever before."

On Thursday, Trump had told Reuters in a telephone interview that he was demanding the right to help select Iran's new supreme leader, to replace Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, killed ​in the war's first day.

Israel pounded the Lebanese capital Beirut on Friday after ordering an unprecedented evacuation ​of the entire southern suburbs of the city, in a major expansion of the war.

It carried out heavy air strikes on Hezbollah-controlled southern suburbs of Beirut and started a "broad-scale" wave of attacks against infrastructure in Tehran, while Iran said it targeted the heart of Tel Aviv with missiles.

headline: Centre releases Rs10b for K-P uplift package
body:
Initial tranche funds security, roads, health, education projects across 37 districts

The federal government has released an initial amount of Rs10 billion to the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's Rs160 billion development package for the province. The funds have been received by the provincial government, according to official sources.

The development package prioritises law and order, healthcare, education, road construction and improvement, and the provision of basic facilities across the province.

According to the proposed allocations, Rs96.971 billion has been earmarked for 12 designated districts, while Rs63.206 billion will be spent on 25 other districts.

A total of 430 development projects will be undertaken in the 12 designated districts. These include seven special projects costing Rs19.27 billion and another 423 schemes for which Rs77.701 billion has been proposed. Both 100-day and 180-day development programmes will also be launched in these districts.

The law and order sector will receive Rs39.19 billion for 62 projects, with particular emphasis on strengthening the operational capacity of police and other law enforcement agencies.

Similarly, Rs3.2 billion has been allocated for 41 health-related projects, while 72 education schemes will be implemented at an estimated cost of Rs12.9 billion.

Three Danesh schools will be established in Bajaur, Kurram and Dera Ismail Khan. In addition, 70 schools will undergo repairs and upgradation, while 409 educational institutions will be solarised to ensure an uninterrupted power supply.

headline: Five dead in South Korea aerospace plant blast
body:
Five people have died and two others were injured on Monday after an explosion and fire on a South Korean production line for rocket propellant at a factory operated by Hanwha Aerospace in the city of Daejeon, officials said.

The two survivors, including one who was badly burned, had escaped from the facility themselves, a fire official told a briefing.

"Authorities have yet to identify the victims because their bodies were severely damaged," a health official told the same briefing.

A fire official said that an explosion had triggered the blaze, though the cause of the blast was still being investigated. The blast appeared to have occurred while water was being used to clean explosive material from tools making rocket propellant, a Hanwha official told a company briefing.

"We bow our heads in apology to the victims and their bereaved families," said Chief Executive Officer Son Jae-il, pledging to cooperate fully with authorities to determine the cause of the accident.

The five dead included two temporary workers in their 20s and all were employed by Hanwha, the company said.

headline: Govt moves to fully digitise passport issuance system
body:
Preparatory work for home delivery of passports in Pakistan, abroad completed, service will be launched soon

The government on Friday decided to transition its passport issuance system to a complete e-passport framework as part of sweeping reforms aimed at modernising immigration services and eliminating fraud.

According to the Interior Ministry, a high-level meeting on Passport and Immigration was held at the headquarters under the chairmanship of Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, where key decisions regarding the digital overhaul of the system were approved.

A principal decision was taken to fully shift passport issuance to e-passports, with the move aimed at reducing fraud and forgery in the passport system. However, no deadline has been announced for the phase-out of existing passports.
