headline: Veena Malik takes off makeup on air to hit back at appearance criticism
body:
Confronts body shaming, challenges societal expectations of female beauty

Actor and television host Veena Malik sparked debate on body shaming and society's obsession with women's appearances after an emotional moment on her morning show.

Responding to online criticism about her physical appearance, Veena removed her high heels and makeup in front of the cameras, challenging those who had been making negative remarks about her looks.

"You guys are only seeing my weight, right? Let me also show you my height and my face," she said while removing her heels. After taking her makeup off with wipes, she stated, "This is my face. Let me show you with my makeup removed so I can give you more reasons to talk about me."

Veena challenged people to turn her natural appearance into another headline, saying, "Now you guys can put out the news. What is Veena Malik without makeup? She is dark, she is fat."

The actor's message went beyond her personal experience with online criticism. Questioning why physical changes should diminish a woman's worth, she said, "Weight has been gained, so now my responsibilities and capabilities are over? Are we just bodies?"

The actor made it clear that her response was not simply about defending herself but about addressing the wider culture of judging women based on their physical appearance. "This isn't just about me and my story but everyone's story and every woman's story," she said.

headline: Drone attacks target Bannu peace jirga
body:
Successive quadcopter strikes injure 10 at tribal gathering

At least 10 people, most of them young, were injured on Sunday morning when two successive quadcopter drone attacks targeted a tribal peace jirga in the Gul Badin Lundi Dak area of Bannu.

Local tribal elders and residents of the Sardi Khel tribe had gathered to discuss the security situation and draw up measures for restoring peace when the first drone struck. A second attack followed shortly afterwards, spreading fear and panic through the area. The injured were immediately shifted to District Headquarters Hospital Bannu, where they are receiving medical treatment.

An initial police report confirmed the incident occurred while participants were consulting on security concerns and steps needed to maintain law and order. The targeting of a peace jirga has raised fresh questions about the safety of tribal elders engaged in local conflict-resolution efforts. No group has so far claimed responsibility, and the motives behind the attacks remain unclear.

In a separate incident, a drone attack was also reported on the residence of Malik Tawani, head of the Hathi Khel Peace Committee. No casualties were reported in that strike.

Earlier, Hathi Khel tribal elders had convened a jirga to consider measures against suspected militants, address security challenges and seek resources for improving law and order. They gave the administration three days to respond to their demands.

headline: Govt decides to end fuel subsidies after sharp decline in global oil prices
body:
Committee agrees to withdraw fuel subsidies after benefit already passed on to consumers

Owing to a sharp decline in global fuel prices, the government on Monday decided to discontinue fuel subsidies provided to motorcyclists, small farmers and public transport.

The development comes after recent reductions in petroleum prices, under which petrol was cut by Rs74 per litre and diesel by Rs67 per litre, bringing them down to Rs299 per litre and Rs311 per litre respectively, following a decline in the international market after the US and Iran reached an agreement to end a conflict that had lasted over three months.

The decision was taken during the seventh meeting of the National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

The committee reviewed the rollout of fuel subsidy for motorcyclists, small farmers, public transport and goods transport across all provinces, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

Noting the sharp decline in global fuel prices and that the benefit had already been passed on to consumers, the committee agreed to discontinue the subsidy, with the prime minister’s approval.

headline: Russian attack near Ukraine’s capital strikes apartment building, killing two and wounding four others
body:
Updated - November 22, 2026 11:00 pm IST - KYIV

Rescuer clears the rubble of an apartment building after a Russian attack in Dymer, Kyiv region, Ukraine on November 22, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP

A Russian attack struck an apartment building in a village near Ukraine’s capital on Sunday (November 22, 2026), killing at least two people and wounding four others, authorities said. Nearly a dozen people were feared trapped beneath the rubble.

The morning strike destroyed the five-storey building in Dymer, which is north of Kyiv. Rescuers have evacuated nine people, including a child, authorities said, while another child was hospitalised with injuries. Search and rescue teams worked to find other survivors. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said 11 people were believed to be trapped.

“When (the explosion came), I literally flipped over in bed,” said Mykola Osadnyi, a relative of some of those trapped. “I live about 200 metres from here. Then we ran over here.” “My father-in-law … was screaming, ‘Save me, I’m burning!’” Mr. Osadnyi said.

“And now we’re just waiting again to see what happens.” Another resident, Olena Kharkavliuk, recounted that “a terrifying sound woke us up, and then there was an explosion”. “My husband and I have been waiting here since about 4 am, because my older daughter’s classmate and her mother are in there,” Ms. Kharkavliuk told AP.

headline: Israel’s Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West Bank
body:
Published - November 23, 2026 05:11 am IST - RAMALLAH

Israeli militant settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank ‌early on Sunday (November 22, 2026), starting fires and scrawling racist graffiti, residents said, prompting an ​accusation of “Jewish terrorism” from the man trying to form an Israeli government.

Also read | Israeli settlers set fire to mosque in occupied West Bank

The attacks come nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his ‌majority. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has been asked to form a government, though his prospects seem little better.

Reuters saw burned-out Palestinian vehicles and walls spray-painted with slogans ‌such as “Revenge” and “Death to Arabs” in villages near Ramallah. No one immediately claimed responsibility and ‌no ⁠injuries were reported.

Mr. Eisenkot called the attacks “Jewish terrorism”, saying that “extremist groups that set ⁠fire to vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security and foreign relations”.

He said the policies of Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, ultra-nationalist ministers in Mr. Netanyahu’s cabinet, had “brought the ​area to the brink of anarchy, ‌and the authorities have yet to address the crisis”.

Mr. Netanyahu has not yet commented, but Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the attacks by a “handful of extremists” and said they are “against our values and do not represent the law-abiding citizens of Judea and Samaria” — the biblical ‌names for the West Bank.

headline: ‘Two rulers, one fort’: Pakistan Minister invokes Humayun, Sher Shah at SCO Civilisational Forum
body:
Updated - November 22, 2026 11:12 am IST - New Delhi

Pakistan's Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Musadik Malik speaks to reporters on the sidelines of the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila, in New Delhi, on November 20, 2026. | Photo Credit: PTI

Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik, in his address at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, invoked Mughal Emperor Humayun and Sher Shah Suri, both associated with the construction of the Purana Qila, and said the old fortress is in itself a story of multiple layers of history.

Editroial | Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi

India is hosting the three-day civilisational summit at the historic precinct of the Purana Qila, which was inaugurated on Friday evening (November 20, 2026) by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the presence of various SCO delegates, including Mr. Malik from Pakistan.

"This [Purana] Qila, where we are sitting, is in itself a story. A fort, whose foundation was laid by Humayun, who had a descent from the Timurid [dynasty] linkage.. came from Central Asia. And, Sher Shah Suri further built on it, who was an Afghan. One wall, two rivals, meaning two rulers and one fort, meaning two layers and one trench," the Pakistan Minister said.

The Prime Minister of Nepal, Balendra Shah, arrived in New Delhi on Sunday (November 22, 2026) afternoon for his first official visit to India. Sources said that Mr. Shah will inaugurate several projects on Monday and is scheduled to hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

headline: Iran says allies China, Russia oppose change in nuclear doctrine
body:
Updated - November 21, 2026 06:27 pm IST - Tehran, Iran

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. File. | Photo Credit: AP

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said China and Russia oppose a change in Tehran’s nuclear doctrine, amid domestic calls for a shift, state media reported.

In an interview published on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Mr. Araghchi told the state-run Iran Daily newspaper that the issue was “broad, serious” and had its own “supporters and opponents”.

“Russia and China are also opposed” to a change in Iran’s doctrine, he added. Both countries have strategic cooperation agreements with Iran.

“What matters is that, up to this point, our doctrine has not changed, and our official positions remain the same as before,” Mr. Araghchi said.

Debate over changing Iran’s nuclear doctrine has resurfaced in the country’s political circles, particularly among hardliners, following wars with Israel and the United States that saw Iranian nuclear facilities come under heavy attack.

Some advocates of a shift argue that it would pave the way for Tehran to develop a nuclear weapon as a deterrent.

Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities.

Last week, the UN nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take “incremental steps” to allow inspectors to return to key facilities, saying such access was “critical”.

headline: Fire at Indonesian candy factory leaves 3 dead, dozens unaccounted for
body:
Updated - November 22, 2026 10:15 am IST - Jakarta

A drone view shows flames engulfing a factory at PT Fonusa Agung Mulia on November 21, 2026 | Photo Credit: Reuters

A fire swept through a candy factory in Indonesia’s Banten province on Saturday (November 22, 2026), leaving three people dead and rescue teams searching for 36 workers who remained unaccounted for, officials said.

The blaze broke out at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Serang district, in Banten province, which borders Jakarta. The factory produces Milkita, an Indonesian brand of milk-based candies and snack products.

The National Search and Rescue Agency released a statement saying that 15 people were rescued alive, including four injured workers. Rescue teams were still searching for the 36 unaccounted-for workers.

“The fire is still burning in several locations, and firefighting teams are continuing extinguishing and cooling operations,” said Rizky Dwianto, an operations official at the Banten Search and Rescue Agency.

He said firefighters from Serang district and Banten province were battling flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the fire began.

Television reports showed flames engulfing the three-story factory, sending thick black smoke into the sky, and causing panic among nearby residents and workers. The floor of the burned-out structure was littered with twisted metal, blackened corrugated iron roofing and other debris.

Outside the factory, anxious relatives waited for news of family members who could not be contacted.

headline: The Rohingya | Vindication for a persecuted people
body:
Updated - November 22, 2026 09:34 am IST

Rohingya refugee children look through a metal net as they gather to watch the live announcement of a verdict by the International Court of Justice in a case accusing Myanmar of committing genocide against the minority Rohingya population on a big screen at a refugee camp in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, on November 19, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

In a first of a kind ruling, the International Court of Justice held on November 19 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State during the military’s “clearance operations” in 2017. This was the first time the ICJ found a state responsible for committing genocide. Nine judges against six voted in favour of the ruling, in a case brought in 2019 by The Gambia.

The court also found that Myanmar failed to prevent genocide by civilians who joined its forces, failed to punish the perpetrators, never enacted the laws that the Genocide Convention requires, and destroyed evidence in breach of the court’s 2020 interim order. It also rejected, by 14 votes to one, the charge that Myanmar directly and publicly incited private persons to commit genocide, but declined to order citizenship for the Rohingya.

headline: Sri Lanka's organised crime bill gets Supreme Court nod
body:
Published - November 21, 2026 10:50 pm IST - Colombo

Sri Lanka's proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill has received the Supreme Court's nod, which ruled that its provisions are "not inconsistent" with the Constitution, Speaker Jagath Wickremaratna told Parliament on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

The Bill, tabled in Parliament on October 20, has drawn criticism from local and international rights groups concerned that its provisions could undermine fundamental rights and grant sweeping powers to law enforcement agencies.

In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality.

The Speaker on Saturday (November 21, 2026) confirmed the Supreme Court's nod for the Bill and listed the clauses it directed Parliament to amend.

"The clauses in the Bill are not inconsistent with the Constitution and may be passed by a simple majority of Parliament, subject to making the amendment at the committee stage," Mr. Wickremaratna said.

He said Clause 6, which allowed the prosecution of an individual who is not a member of a criminal gang, should be deleted, citing the Court's directions.

Criticism of the Bill has centred on its broad definition of organised crime and provisions that could allow authorities to identify individuals as gang members based on their appearance or associations.

headline: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
body:
Updated - November 22, 2026 12:20 pm IST - Beijing

The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed. With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia.

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.”

The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

headline: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties resume talks to form Israel government
body:
Updated - November 22, 2026 10:58 pm IST - Herzliya

Delegations from Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud began their meeting at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks on Sunday (November 15, 2026). | Photo Credit: Reuters

The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over whether to form a coalition government, with Mr. Netanyahu’s party insisting on keeping his main policies.

Delegations from Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud began their meeting at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

A former Chief of Staff of the army, Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6, 2026, to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the October 2026 elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.

His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.

Mr. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel.

headline: Iraq fire at Basra power station kills at least four, injures 30
body:
Updated - November 22, 2026 01:04 pm IST - Basra, Iraq

At least four people were killed ​and 30 injured in ‌a fire at a power ​station in southern Iraq ⁠on Saturday (November 21, 2026), with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.

Civil defence ‌teams brought the fire at the Hartha ‌power station north of Basra ‌under ⁠control after firefighters responded ⁠to the incident, Iraq’s state news agency, INA, reported.

The fire spread to neighbouring ​houses and ‌forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.

The Hartha station ‌has an installed generating ​capacity of 800 megawatts but had been operating at ⁠around 400 megawatts before the fire, they said.

There was no ‌immediate official information on the cause of the fire or the extent of the damage, INA reported.

Iraq’s electricity infrastructure has long struggled ‌with decades of underinvestment, inadequate maintenance ​, and an inability to meet peak demand, particularly during ⁠the extremely hot summer months. Fires ⁠and technical failures at substations and power facilities have ‌previously disrupted electricity supplies and caused widespread outages.

headline: Central California concert shooting: Nine people shot; one in critical condition
body:
Updated - November 23, 2026 10:43 am IST - Sacramento (U.S.)

Image used for representational purposes only. | Photo Credit: AP

Nine people were shot at a concert in central California, leaving one person critically injured with a chest injury, the local sheriff said Sunday (November 22).

The shooting broke out around 7:30 p.m. Saturday (November 21) at a concert attended by about 150 people in Strathmore, a small town in Tulare County, a mountainous region in the centre of the state, the county sheriff's department said in a statement. An unspecified number of suspects opened fire on the crowd. No arrests were announced.

One 26-year-old man was shot in the chest and required surgery. He remained in critical condition, the sheriff's department said. Two other victims, ages 19 and 22, also required surgery, while six people sustained minor injuries.

Authorities said that they believe the shooting “may be gang-related” but didn't elaborate. The show in the town of roughly 3,000 people featured performers from neighbouring states, the department said.

The department didn't immediately respond to emailed questions seeking further details but said there was no longer any immediate threat to the public.

headline: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO, says NYT
body:
Updated - November 23, 2026 11:06 am IST - WASHINGTON

The Huangpu river flows past the window of a dining room at Pujiang Huaiyang Cuisine restaurant, where restaurant staff said Alice Huang and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dined in 2025, in Shanghai, on November 12, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

Alice Huang, the Chinese woman at the heart of Nvidia’s recent scandal, kept in contact with an official ​from China’s top spy agency for more than a year during ‌her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York ​Times reported on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

Alice Huang was in ⁠touch with an officer from China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, ‌citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

Spokespersons for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and the Chinese Embassy ‌in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for ‌comment. ⁠Reuters has not been able to reach Alice ⁠Huang for comment.

Alice Huang previously led Singapore-based Megaspeed International, an important Nvidia customer that once accounted for billions in Nvidia chip sales.

U.S. authorities have been investigating Megaspeed ​since 2024 over concerns it smuggled ‌Nvidia’s advanced AI chips to China.

Sunday’s (November 22, 2026) report comes as US officials have cast doubt on initial suggestions that Alice Huang was a spy, as the newspaper reported last month.

headline: Democrats win U.S. Congress in midterm rout of U.S. President Donald Trump
body:
Updated - November 23, 2026 10:40 am IST - Washington

US Senator Jon Ossoff embraces a supporter as he greets them during an election night rally after winning reelection in the U.S. midterm elections, in Atlanta, Georgia, on November 3, 2026 | Photo Credit: Reuters

Democrats won full control of the U.S. Congress in a sweeping midterm rout on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.

Also Read: Democrats clinch a historic House majority of at least 258 seats, largest since 1992

The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Mr. Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency.

The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Mr. Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president.

Mr. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times: “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats.”

But minutes later on social media the 80-year-old signaled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.”

The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night.
